hook: Houdini’s diary reveals performances from 1897‑1899—yet most fans never saw it.

sections.voiceover: Houdini’s diary reveals performances from 1897‑1899—yet most fans never saw it.
sections.visual_cue: Close‑up of an opened travel diary page showing the years 1897‑1899.
b_roll: Historical photograph of Houdini on stage.

sections.voiceover: John Cox announced on Wild About Harry that Houdini’s diary covers 1897‑1899. Which journals, dated 1898 and 1916, appeared at the Jewish Museum?
sections.visual_cue: Series of three shots: blog screenshot, book cover, museum exhibit label.
b_roll: Display case at the Jewish Museum

sections.voiceover: But the diaries confirm Bess Houdini’s pivotal role in his tours.
sections.visual_cue: Portrait of Bess Houdini beside a stage‑plan diagram.
b_roll: Photo of Bess Houdini with Harry backstage.

sections.voiceover: In 2011 the Jewish Museum unveiled the 1898 and 1916 journals, closing gaps. Combined with the 376‑page “Escaping Obscurity,” scholars now have an illustrated timeline.
sections.visual_cue: Timeline graphic overlaying museum exhibit, then page flips, then book spread.
b_roll: Museum display of the two journals

sections.voiceover: Houdini’s diary finally lifts the veil on his rise.
sections.visual_cue: Slow zoom out from the diary to a silhouette of Houdini escaping chains.
b_roll: Silhouette animation of Houdini’s famous escape act.
